stories.headline: Anthropic in Talks to Raise $30B–$50B at Up to $950B Valuation

key_facts.fact: Anthropic is in talks to raise between $30 billion and $50 billion in a round that would value it at up to $950 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Sources: Anthropic is in talks to raise between $30B and $50B in a funding round that would value it at up to $950B (Mike Isaac/New York Times)

key_facts.fact: Bloomberg reports the talks involve at least $30 billion in fresh financing at a valuation of more than $900 billion, not including the new investment, with the round potentially closing by month-end.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic PBC is in early talks with investors to raise at least $30 billion in fresh financing... The Claude maker is in discussions to raise the new capital at a valuation of more than $900 billion, not including the investment... The round is expected to close as soon as the end of this month.

key_facts.fact: The talks come less than three months after Anthropic's $30 billion round closed in February 2026 at a $380 billion valuation.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic, meanwhile, was valued at $380 billion as of February.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic's annualized revenue has reached $30 billion, up from roughly $10 billion in 2025 and $9 billion at the end of 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: The company said earlier this month that it has reached $30 billion in annualized revenue. It generated roughly $10 billion in revenue last year.

key_facts.fact: A $950B valuation would surpass OpenAI's most recent public round at $852 billion post-money in late March 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI was valued at $852 billion in late March after closing a record-breaking $122 billion funding round.

stories.headline: Recursive Superintelligence Raises $650M+ at $4B for Self-Improving AI

key_facts.fact: Recursive Superintelligence has raised over $650 million from venture firms including Google Ventures (GV) and Greycroft, plus chipmakers Nvidia and AMD.
key_facts.excerpt: Recursive Superintelligence, founded by former Google, Meta and OpenAI researchers, is part of a growing effort to automate the creation of artificial intelligence. The company has raised over $650 million from venture capital firms including Google Ventures and Greycroft and the chip-making giants Nvidia and AMD.

key_facts.fact: The round values the four-month-old London-incorporated company at $4 billion pre-money; the prior FT report in April pegged at least $500 million committed and noted oversubscription could push the total to $1 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: The financing values the London-incorporated company at $4 billion before new capital and was so oversubscribed it could eventually reach $1 billion.

key_facts.fact: The founding team includes Richard Socher (former Salesforce chief scientist), Tim Rocktäschel (UCL professor and former director of Google DeepMind's Open-Endedness group), and former OpenAI researchers Josh Tobin, Jeff Clune, and Tim Shi, with about 20 staff overall.
key_facts.excerpt: The four-month-old London-incorporated startup names co-founders from Google DeepMind and OpenAI, including Berlin-born UCL professor Tim Rocktäschel and former OpenAI researchers Josh Tobin, Jeff Clune, and Tim Shi.

key_facts.fact: The company's stated goal is to automate the entire AI development pipeline — evaluation, data selection, training, post-training, and research direction — without human intervention at each step.
key_facts.excerpt: Recursive Superintelligence, which hasn't officially launched yet, wants to build an AI system that keeps improving itself without any human involvement.

stories.headline: Isomorphic Labs Raises $2.1B Series B Led by Thrive for AI Drug Design

key_facts.fact: Isomorphic Labs announced a $2.1 billion Series B funding round led by Thrive Capital, with existing backers Alphabet and GV alongside new investors MGX, Temasek, CapitalG, and the UK Sovereign AI Fund.
key_facts.excerpt: LONDON, May 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Isomorphic Labs, an AI-first drug design and development company, today announced it has raised $2.1 Billion in Series B funding... The financing round is led by Thrive Capital, and includes participation from existing backers Alphabet and GV alongside new investors MGX, Temasek, CapitalG, and the UK Sovereign AI Fund.

key_facts.fact: The capital will fund Isomorphic's AI drug design engine (IsoDDE) and expand its pipeline of therapeutic programs toward clinical trials.
key_facts.excerpt: The new capital will be used for the continued development and deployment of Isomorphic Labs' AI drug design engine (IsoDDE), accelerating and expanding its pipeline of therapeutic programs towards the clinic.

key_facts.fact: Isomorphic was spun out of Google DeepMind in 2021 and previously raised $600 million in its first external round in March 2025, also led by Thrive.
key_facts.excerpt: Isomorphic was founded in 2021 as a spin-off from Google DeepMind, an AI research lab acquired by Alphabet in 2014... The London-based company raised $600 million in its first funding round last year, also led by Thrive Capital.

key_facts.fact: The company aims to start its first clinical trials by the end of 2026, a delay from CEO Demis Hassabis's earlier target of having AI-designed drugs in trials by the end of 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: The company now [aims to start] its first clinical trials by the end of 2026 — a delay from the CEO's earlier target of having AI-designed drugs in trials by the end of 2025.

stories.headline: Anduril Raises $5B Series H at $61B, Doubling Valuation in Under a Year

key_facts.fact: Anduril Industries raised a $5 billion Series H led by Thrive Capital and Andreessen Horowitz at a $61 billion valuation.
key_facts.excerpt: Anduril raised a $5B Series H led by Thrive and a16z at a $61B valuation, up from $30.5B in June 2025, taking its total funding to $6.82B, and may IPO in 2027— The start-up, which makes A.I.-backed weapons, was valued at $61 billion in the financing round, double what it was a year ago.

key_facts.fact: The new valuation roughly doubles the $30.5 billion mark set in Anduril's June 2025 Series G, which raised $2.5 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: In June, the company completed its Series G, securing $2.5 billion and achieving a valuation of more than $30.5 billion.

key_facts.fact: The Series H brings Anduril's total funding to $6.82 billion; the company is reportedly weighing an IPO as soon as 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: taking its total funding to $6.82B, and may IPO in 2027

key_facts.fact: Initial reports in March 2026 had Anduril seeking $4 billion at a $60 billion valuation, with potential to bring in as much as $8 billion of capital.
key_facts.excerpt: A previous report from Bloomberg said the new round could bring as much as $8 billion of capital into the company.

stories.headline: Anthropic in Advanced Talks to Buy SDK Generator Stainless for $300M+

key_facts.fact: Anthropic is in advanced talks to acquire New York-based Stainless, a startup that helps developers generate SDKs from APIs, for at least $300 million.
key_facts.excerpt: Source: Anthropic is in advanced talks to acquire New York-based Stainless, which helps developers generate SDKs from APIs, for at least $300M (The Information)

key_facts.fact: Stainless's SDK-generation software is currently used by Anthropic's rivals, including OpenAI and Google; OpenAI adopted Stainless after struggling to maintain its own SDK.
key_facts.excerpt: Stainless, founded 4 years ago, has provided software that uses AI to automatically generate software development kits (SDKs)... OpenAI previously developed its own SDK, but adopted Stainless because maintenance was difficult and resource burdens were high.

key_facts.fact: Stainless has also built dedicated software linking with Model Context Protocol (MCP), the standard Anthropic launched in November 2024.
key_facts.excerpt: Stainless also built dedicated software that links with MCP (Model Context Protocol), which Anthropic launched in November 2024.

key_facts.fact: The deal would extend a six-month M&A run for Anthropic following the December 2025 acquisition of developer-tools startup Bun and subsequent purchases of computer-use startup Vercept and AI biotech startup Coefficient Bio.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic has recently been aggressive on mergers and acquisitions over the past 6 months. After its first acquisition of developer tools startup Bun in December last year, it acquired computer use startup Vercept and AI biotech startup Coefficient Bio in succession.

stories.headline: Google DeepMind Unveils Gemini-Powered 'Magic Pointer' for Chrome and Googlebook

key_facts.fact: Google DeepMind published a research blog and experimental demos for an AI-enabled mouse pointer powered by Gemini that aims to understand both what the user is pointing at and why it matters.
key_facts.excerpt: We've been exploring new AI-powered capabilities to help the pointer not only understand what it's pointing at, but also why it matters to the user... Today, we're outlining the underlying principles guiding our thinking on future user interfaces, and sharing experimental demos of an AI-enabled pointer, powered by Gemini.

key_facts.fact: Two interactive demos are live in Google AI Studio: one for editing images by pointing and talking, and one for finding places on a map.
key_facts.excerpt: you could visit Google AI Studio to edit an image or find places on the map, just by pointing and speaking.

key_facts.fact: The pointer is being integrated into Gemini in Chrome — users can select products on a page and ask Gemini to compare, or point to visualize a new couch in their living room — and into the upcoming 'Googlebook' laptop as 'Magic Pointer'.
key_facts.excerpt: We are now integrating these principles to reimagine pointing in Chrome and our new Googlebook laptop experience... Similarly, we'll soon roll out Magic Pointer in Googlebook, allowing users to harness Gemini at their fingertips for a more intuitive experience.

key_facts.fact: Google announced the Magic Pointer alongside Googlebook, a new laptop category 'built from the ground up for Gemini intelligence' set to launch in fall 2026, in partnership with OEMs including Dell and HP.
key_facts.excerpt: We are introducing Googlebook, a new category of laptops built from the ground up for Gemini intelligence. These devices feature the Magic Pointer for contextual suggestions and custom widgets to help you organize your tasks. Keep an eye on googlebook.com for more updates before the devices launch this fall.

stories.headline: Anthropic Launches 12 Claude Legal Plugins and MCP Connectors for Law Firms

key_facts.fact: Anthropic announced a dozen new Claude plugins targeted at attorneys, law students and others in the legal sector, including a 'commercial counsel' tool aimed at vendor agreement review and a study tool for the bar exam.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic on Tuesday announced a dozen new tools, or plugins, intended for attorneys, law students and others in the legal sector. One feature, called 'commercial counsel,' is meant to take on work like reviewing vendor agreements; another tool is intended to help with studying for the bar exam.

key_facts.fact: The 12 plugins span commercial, privacy, corporate, employment, product and AI governance, covering document search/review, case-law research, deposition preparation and drafting; they include 'employment counsel', 'litigation associate' and a 'law student' bar-exam tool.
key_facts.excerpt: The twelve plug-ins span legal fields including commercial, privacy, corporate, employment, product, and AI governance, and address functions such as document search and review, case law research, deposition preparation, and document drafting.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic also released MCP connectors that link Claude to leading legal software platforms, including Thomson Reuters' Westlaw and Practical Law, Box for document management, Everlaw for e-discovery and Docusign for e-signature.
key_facts.excerpt: Box — for cloud-based document and file management... Everlaw — for cloud-based electronic discovery... Docusign — for [contract] management and electronic signature workflows... Thomson Reuters confirmed that its Westlaw-enabled AI platform CoCounsel Legal has been integrated with Claude via MCP.

key_facts.fact: All twelve plugins are available to existing paying Claude customers and can run inside Claude Cowork or be embedded into a firm's existing systems.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic said the new tools can be deployed directly inside its Claude Cowork environment or embedded into a law firm's existing systems. All twelve plug-ins are available to existing paying Claude customers.
